* 2. VersionedStorage
:PROPERTIES:

:FILE: src/graphden/versioning/storage/core.clj
:LINE: 990
:MINS: 12.6

The decorator record itself. It implements every storage protocol, delegating non-versioned entities straight to the base storage and intercepting versioned ones — reads resolve to a branch view, writes append version rows. Every method is a two-line dispatch: read this for the SHAPE, then follow the versioned arm into its own function. Grasp this structure before anything else here.

The list-item position-collision guard, now in a shared ~uniqueness~ namespace so BOTH the write path (~core~) and the merge path (~merge~) enforce it without a require cycle. A cross-branch base index on ~(binding-id, position)~ would wrongly block divergence, so per-branch uniqueness is enforced here in the resolved view instead — a subtle invariant the write path defends with an advisory lock. Fn names follow the same doctrine: ~check-fn-name-collision!~ just below replaced the raw ~UNIQUE (namespace_id, name)~, whose soft-deleted identities blocked their names forever.

* 12. purgeable-identity-ids
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: versioning/purgeable-identity-ids
:FILE: src/graphden/versioning/storage/core.clj
:LINE: 202
:MINS: 3.8
:END:

Delete has TWO modes, and this guard is the heart of the hard one. User-facing deletes tombstone (a version row with ~:deleted-at~, so descendants hide the entity too); sync + rollback hard-delete. A hard delete used to drop only the branch's version rows — the surviving versionless identity became a GHOST that a later re-mint of the same deterministic id revived through the update path, content-equal, invisible on every list read (the 2026-07-20 route-vanish incident). Now the identity row goes too, but ONLY when no other branch retains a version and no child identity still references it — per-branch isolation stays intact.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/versioning/storage/core.clj::(defn- purgeable-identity-ids][src/graphden/versioning/storage/core.clj:202]]

* 13. repoint-refs!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: versioning/repoint-refs!
:FILE: src/graphden/versioning/identity_repair.clj
:LINE: 52
:MINS: 3.8
:END:

The identity-plane repair primitives for the OTHER ghost source: a package fn's id is ~uuid-v5(ns-path, name)~, so a namespace move mints a new id and abandons the old row with every ref still aimed at it. ~repoint-refs!~ fills refs in place across BOTH planes (identity and every branch's version rows); ~purge-fn-subgraph!~ below then removes the abandoned subgraph. The sync-time reconciler (~packages.sync/reconcile-moved-identities!~) runs them after every package sync, and the operator tool ~graphden.dev.integrity~ delegates to the same two. Its REMOVAL side asks ~inbound-refs-many~ with ~:live-only?~ — only the newest version of a row on a live branch counts as a ref, never the create-time identity row or a superseded version — because those two kept every retired chain a live fn had ever referenced pinned forever (472 leftovers on a two-month-old instance, 2026-09-04).

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/versioning/identity_repair.clj::(defn repoint-refs!][src/graphden/versioning/identity_repair.clj:52]]

The DISPLAY model over diff-branches (diff v2): entries grouped under the fn that owns them (list-items chain through their binding), per-field before/after pairs for modified rows, and batch name-resolution for slots and fn-typed refs. The editor's compare mode (inspector diff panel + Review dialog) client-renders THIS shape from the :diff-branches-view base-fn's JSON endpoint; the v1 API keeps the flat wire shape.

* 17. merge-branch!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: versioning/merge-branch!
:FILE: src/graphden/versioning/storage/merge.clj
:LINE: 657
:MINS: 8.9
:END:

The merge itself: assert conflicts are resolved, then atomically write ONE ~branch-merge~ record — which makes the source's versions visible through resolution, copying no rows — plus any resolution overrides. The payoff step tying resolution and conflict detection together.

Read it in three parts: validate (conflicts resolved, approval policy satisfied), write — the single ~branch-merge~ row plus any resolution overrides, in one transaction — then report, including ~skipped-as-branch-local~ right below it: the rows a merge deliberately does NOT carry across.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/versioning/storage/merge.clj::(defn merge-branch!][src/graphden/versioning/storage/merge.clj:657]]

* 18. merge-transitively!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: versioning/merge-transitively!
:FILE: src/graphden/versioning/merge/core.clj
:LINE: 263
:MINS: 4.4

What makes a merge transitive: the storage layer surfaces only the source's OWN rows and refuses when the source inherits from a branch the target lacks, so this layer merges those branches in first — root-most first, each through the same policy gate a direct merge would face — then the source, and reports the steps as ~:merged-first~. docs/VERSIONING.md § Known gaps.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/versioning/merge/core.clj::(defn merge-transitively!][src/graphden/versioning/merge/core.clj:263]]

* 19. validate-approval-policy!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: versioning/validate-approval-policy!
:FILE: src/graphden/versioning/merge/core.clj
:LINE: 212
:MINS: 3.1
:END:

Merge GOVERNANCE — the code-review gate. When the target branch sets ~:required-approvals~, a merge into it is refused (~:branch/approval-required~, 409) until the proposal has enough VALID approvals: distinct, non-stale, BOUND to this exact merge target (~target-branch-id~), and — when the target names a restrictive ~:approver-ids~ — from that allow-list. Counting is pure/open-core (WHO may approve was enforced when each ~:branch-approval~ row was written, and re-checked here so a tightened policy or a wrong-target approval can't slip through); the live merge base-fn calls this right after the ~:forbid-invalid?~ gate. This is how 'protect main, land via reviewed merges' is enforced.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/versioning/merge/core.clj::(defn validate-approval-policy!][src/graphden/versioning/merge/core.clj:212]]

* 20. branch-content-stamp
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: versioning/branch-content-stamp
:FILE: src/graphden/versioning/merge/core.clj
:LINE: 141
:MINS: 1.6
:END:

The stale-dismissal fingerprint: a branch's own version rows reduced to ~count|max(created-at)~. An approval records the source's stamp at approval time; any later edit APPENDS a version row, so the stamp advances and ~count-valid-approvals~ stops counting the now- stale approval — GitHub's 'dismiss stale reviews on a new push', expressed as a monotonic content signal rather than an event hook.

* 21. bump!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: versioning/bump!
:FILE: src/graphden/storage/postgres/graph_epoch.clj
:LINE: 97
:MINS: 2.4
:END:

The graph EPOCH — freshness as a comparison, not an imperative. Every graph-shaped write bumps this sequence BEFORE writing; the router's fetch-time check (~validate-graph-epoch!~) heals any cached ctx whose eager invalidation was skipped — a client abort mid-request, a write path with no NOTIFY, a lost NOTIFY. The eager delta machinery and NOTIFY remain pure latency optimizations, which is what their docstrings always claimed.

Builds a fresh live ~ExecutionContext~ whose storage is a ~VersionedStorage~ rewrapped at the requested branch, with its own compiled-registry and graph-cache atoms — and (2026-08-31) its own RICH-TYPES SLICE, forked from the base's view at build time and bound as the registry override for the ctx's compiles and every request dispatched to it. This is how a branch gets its own executor without re-sharding the graph.

* 23. dispatch*
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: versioning/dispatch*
:FILE: src/graphden/system/branch_router.clj
:LINE: 1435
:MINS: 8.6
:END:

The top-level Ring dispatch: extract the branch ref (header or query), resolve it to a branch-id, and route the request to that branch's lazily-built handler (400 on an unknown branch). Where a live request finally lands in the correct per-branch context. Its public wrapper ~dispatch~ first short-circuits ~/livez~ — the one registry-independent liveness path — so a pod busy on a full recompile still answers its probe.
